nodes.title: Analysis-quality bench: 84 synthetic keyed calls (12 templates x 6 industries, plus Tamil-, Bengali- and Marathi-English) and a 36-call cross-call slice with 3 planted objection themes, scored by code with Wilson 95% intervals

Analytics quality is measured by a bench whose keys are hand-written per template and whose scoring is code only, through the real path (signed ingest, then post-call analysis or insight). Reason-code accuracy is split into model-refined calls and calls decided by code
nodes.rationale: Inherited law: a model never grades. Splitting the reason code stops code-decided calls (no answer, opt-out, crisis) from inflating the model's number.
nodes.reverse_if: A human review of real calls finds the template keys miss how people actually talk; then add keyed real (consented, de-identified) transcripts beside the synthetic ones.

nodes.title: The deterministic caller-signal floor (shared/safety callerSignals) catches 6 of 9 opt-outs in the bench. It misses all 3 regional phrasings (Tamil-, Bengali- and Marathi-English 'do not call me again, remove my number')
nodes.method: analysis bench (fake oracle, so the result is independent of any model): callerSignals(text).optOut over the caller lines of the 9 opt-out keyed calls

nodes.title: A Tamil-, Bengali- or Marathi-English caller's 'do not call me again' is not caught by the live floor, so the runtime may emit no opt_out moment. Suppression then depends on post-call analysis catching it
nodes.mitigation: Safety module: add regional opt-out phrasings to the floor lexicon (cases.json), with the bench's 3 lines as cases; the post-call analysis opt_out moment remains the second check.

nodes.title: How accurate are per-call analysis and cross-call insight on a real model? The bench has only run with the scripted oracle (CI)
nodes.closes_when: The integrator runs `node --import tsx product/scripts/analysis-bench.ts` with VP_LLM_ANALYSIS_* set (1 request a second, token cap) and files the analysis-bench.json numbers as measure.* nodes.

nodes.title: The analysis contract is written as shapes: the model may name CONV_* codes only, null outcome only when no PERSON line bears on the question, every agreeing PERSON line is a commitment, and the outcome carries a confidence
nodes.rationale: The real-model bench showed three miss classes. Mini gave null outcomes on wrong-person, complaint and opt-out calls; found 7 of 21 commitments; and named END_HANDED_OFF, an engine code, on 2 complaint calls. The changes are class-level, from the template pattern of the misses, not tuned item by item. A mutation test proves the CONV_* guard is what stops an engine code.
nodes.reverse_if: The TEST split on a real model shows no gain over the old contract on outcome and commitment recall, or a loss elsewhere.

nodes.title: The analysis model is chosen per workspace from a curated list: single, or tiered (a cheaper first pass that escalates failed, outcome-less or low-confidence calls to a stronger model). No default model is chosen in code
nodes.rationale: Computed for a 3-minute call: mini about ₹0.073, GPT-4.1 about ₹0.38, against a ₹0.17 budget. Tiered costs ₹0.073 plus e x ₹0.38, so it stays under budget while the escalation rate e is below 26%. The bench's no-outcome rate for mini was 16.7%.
nodes.reverse_if: The TEST split shows tiered accuracy significantly below GPT-4.1-only, or a real-traffic escalation rate of 26% or more.

nodes.title: Analysis bench on real models (integrator's run, older contract): outcome 70/84 (mini) vs 84/84 (GPT-4.1); moment recall 57/72 vs 67/72; quotes grounded 230/230 and 277/277; cross-call themes 3/3 on both; ₹0.048 vs ₹0.263 per call
nodes.method: product/scripts/analysis-bench.ts at 1 request a second on Azure models; scored by code against hand-written keys

events.details: Built the analysis-quality bench (product/scripts/analysis-bench.ts, cases in product/scripts/analysis-bench/cases.ts) and its CI test (product/tests/calls-bench.test.ts, 3 tests: set integrity, oracle smoke, and a wrong model scoring low). With the oracle over all 84 calls, every model-driven field is 100% (as expected for an oracle), the grounding check drops each planted invented quote (210/288 kept), and cross-call recall is 3/3. One model-independent finding: the floor's opt-out recall is 6/9, missing all regional phrasings. Gates: tsc clean, ui-contract 0 missing, full suite 403/403 on a fresh database. Not run: a real model.

Calls changes:
- The bench is split DEV/TEST, 42/42, stratified so every template and language is on both sides.
- The analysis contract is rewritten as shapes. Engine codes are refused from the model (mutation-checked). Outcome null is allowed only when no PERSON line bears on the question. Commitments are every agreeing PERSON line. The outcome carries a confidence.
- Per-workspace single or tiered analysis model (migration 0604, analysis.settings.get / analysis.model.set). Escalation on a failed pass, no outcome, or low confidence; a cost line per pass.
- The bench's cross-call slice is seeded as the product writes calls (turns, outcome rows, end reason), so goals come from graded outcomes.
- Cost model in product/server/modules/calls/ANALYSIS-COST.md.
Verified: 6 tier tests, 4 bench tests; full suite 418/418 on a fresh database.
Not verified: the new contract on a real model (no keys in this sandbox); the integrator runs TEST.
